tweets.text:
Solo Satoshi was born at the lowest part of my life. I had just gotten fired for the first time ever. All I knew was hard work since the age of 15 years old, running a pet store by myself for 12+ hours a day. The sudden stop in productivity on the day to day basis was a spiritual awakening for me, once the realization set in that I was just a number to my employer and most of the world. 

Fortunately, being the chameleon I am, I adapted and overcame like I’ve spent most of my life doing. Life never dealt me a fair deck of cards since I’ve been on my own since 17 years old. Being on your own at such young age will teach you life lessons that large amounts of money could never buy.

Solo Satoshi was started with the small person in mind. The forgotten ones. The ones who really matter. The majority!

The Bitcoin mining industry has been ceased and taken over by wealthy elites who have overstayed their welcome in an attempt to take over the Bitcoin Network and own majority of the hashrate (70%+). This was unacceptable to both me and Hunter, thus the birth of Solo Satoshi began.

Solo Satoshi is a small business with just 3 employees. We are a family run business. We are in tune with the community and we have a strict moral compass which we abide by daily. Contrary to popular belief, we have only been a business for 7 short months and have achieved incredible things as a family and a team.

There have been many days that our team has stayed up 24+ hours to ensure our customers packages made it out in a timely matter, because we realize that without our supporters and the trust of the community we are nothing.

Our number one priority is to ensure that every customer feels special and has their needs met within a timely manner, or you get 100% of your money back. We believe in the delivery of only the highest quality products and hold manufacturers globally to that same standard.

Unfortunately, there comes a time in every businesses journey, especially when experiencing hyper growth, when enemies can be easily made, especially when you refuse to bend the knee. That being said, Solo Satoshi does not bend the knee to any centralized authority regardless of money, power, or connections. We were born with attitude. Pissed off that Bitcoin - freedom money, is becoming centralized. 

To all of the open source developers, manufacturers, and distributors globally: we appreciate every opportunity that we’ve ever been given, and appreciate you here throughout our journey. We are ready to fight till the death for what we believe in. We will never surrender to anyone.

We do this for our families future. We do this for the community. We do this for Bitcoin. We do this for FREEDOM. We are here to stay!

“To win any battle, you must fight as if you are already dead”
- Miyamoto Musashi

tweets.text:
Liang Wenfeng - Founder of DeepSeek

Liang was born in 1985 in Guangdong, China, to a modest family.

His father was a school teacher, and his values of discipline and education greatly influenced Liang.

Liang pursued his studies at Zhejiang University, earning a master’s degree in engineering in 2010.

His research focused on low-cost camera tracking algorithms, showcasing his early interest in practical AI applications.

In 2015, he co-founded High-Flyer, a quantitative hedge fund powered by AI-driven algorithms.

The fund grew rapidly, managing over $100 billion, but he was not content with just the financial success.

He envisioned using AI to solve larger, more impactful problems beyond the finance industry.

In 2023, Liang founded DeepSeek to create cutting-edge AI models for broader use.

Unlike many tech firms, DeepSeek prioritized research and open-source innovation over commercial apps.

Liang hired top PhDs from universities like Peking and Tsinghua, focusing on talent with passion and vision.

To address US chip export restrictions, Liang preemptively secured 10,000 Nvidia GPUs.

This strategic move ensured DeepSeek could compete with global leaders like OpenAI.

DeepSeek's AI models achieved high performance at a fraction of the cost of competitors.

Liang turned down a $10 billion acquisition offer, stating that DeepSeek’s goal was to advance AI, not just profit.

He advocates for originality in China’s tech industry, emphasizing innovation over imitation.

He argued that closed-source technologies only temporarily delay competitors and emphasized the importance of open innovation.

Liang credits his father’s dedication to education for inspiring his persistence and values.

He believes AI should serve humanity broadly, not just the wealthy or elite industries.

tweets.text:
For almost 20 years, I've been on X/Twitter.

The platform has been an invaluable connector to information & people around the world.

But the value exchange has been largely one way: I've consumed content but created very little in return.

Starting now, I want to change that.

I'm a three-time founder who has spent 30+ years in Silicon Valley building and investing in innovative tech companies. So much of my journey has been enabled by the support and guidance of others.

After decades of learning from others, it's time to pay it forward.

So if we haven't met yet, I'm Nirav Tolia, and I:

• Co-founded @Nextdoor in 2010 and returned in 2024 as CEO to drive our company's turnaround. We're reimagining the power of local, real-world communities in an increasingly disconnected world.

• Started in Silicon Valley as an undergrad @Stanford in the early 90s. That led to the lottery ticket of joining Yahoo! as employee #84, where I experienced first-hand the early days of the dot-com boom (and bust).

• Created three consumer internet companies (two went public), raised hundreds of millions in private funding, hired hundreds of employees, and developed a deep network spanning SV, Texas, and Europe.

• Invested in and advised dozens of companies as an angel investor, Chairman of Hedosophia, and a Guest Shark on @ABCSharkTank. Sitting on the other side of the table only reinforces my love of entrepreneurship.

• Organized scores of dinners with accomplished tech CEOs and leaders in many diverse fields. No press, no agenda — just a sincere desire for authentic connection and raw conversations about mutual challenges.

Yes, I've been fortunate to experience a unique level of business success. But I've also experienced the worst kind of heartache, despair, and failure. In fact, my belief is that the best insights don't come from the good times, they come from the necessity of learning from the bad ones.

And it's those learnings that I want to share, honestly and humbly.

This will include the unfiltered truth about building @Nextdoor the second time around, as well as all of my experiences around entrepreneurship, investing, community, and everything else I've experienced in my 53 years.

Please follow me @niravtolia for more!
